{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java",
      "line": 483,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Token ID matcher does not verify the expected grant prefix",
      "body": "In isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut is expected to be encoded in the new token ID format 'ssttgg:uuid', where the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the prefix. The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut. This is both the wrong substring and inverted logic, so it accepts token IDs whose actual grant prefix does not match the expected grant and can fail only accidentally. It may also throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for short prefixes. As a result, the updated event assertions do not validate the encoded grant type."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java",
      "line": 73,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId",
      "body": "AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, \"Null rawTokenId not allowed\") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId can therefore be stored. Later, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId concatenates the raw token ID into the encoded token ID, which can produce an ID ending in ':null' or cause failures in consumers expecting a valid opaque token ID."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 33,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "New getShortcut method is a breaking SPI change",
      "body": "OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing SPI interface. Adding String getShortcut() as an abstract method without a default implementation breaks existing custom grant-type factory implementations at compile time and can cause AbstractMethodError at runtime for binary extensions. If this is required, the compatibility impact should be explicit; otherwise a default method should be provided."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java",
      "line": 87,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Public Context copy constructor removed",
      "body": "The diff removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context). This is a source and binary compatibility break for any extension code that copied an existing Context. If this type is considered stable enough for custom grant implementations, the removal should be avoided or clearly documented as a breaking change."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java",
      "line": 54,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Lightweight-token check depends on session-context client",
      "body": "getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the token is lightweight by calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...). Token creation already has a client available via TokenManager.initToken and the client session. If a caller creates an access token without setting the client in the session context, or if the context client differs from the token's client, this can throw NullPointerException or encode the wrong token type. The decision should use the client associated with the token being created."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but format requires exactly 2 characters",
      "body": "The Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut says it returns 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes and decodes exactly two characters for the grant type field. Custom grant factories following this Javadoc could return three-character shortcuts, producing token IDs that cannot be parsed. The documentation should state that the shortcut must be exactly two characters."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java",
      "line": 113,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Lazily registered grant shortcuts can overwrite existing mappings",
      "body": "Startup validates grant shortcut uniqueness by comparing the sizes of grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts. However, getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily insert mappings for grant factories discovered later without re-validating uniqueness or format. A newly discovered grant with a conflicting shortcut can silently overwrite the shortcut-to-grant mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type while still encoding successfully."
    }

findings.title: Token ID matcher does not verify the expected grant prefix
findings.body: In isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut is expected to be encoded in the new token ID format 'ssttgg:uuid', where the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the prefix. The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut. This is both the wrong substring and inverted logic, so it accepts token IDs whose actual grant prefix does not match the expected grant and can fail only accidentally. It may also throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for short prefixes. As a result, the updated event assertions do not validate the encoded grant type.

findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId can therefore be stored. Later, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId concatenates the raw token ID into the encoded token ID, which can produce an ID ending in ':null' or cause failures in consumers expecting a valid opaque token ID.

findings.title: New getShortcut method is a breaking SPI change
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an existing SPI interface. Adding String getShortcut() as an abstract method without a default implementation breaks existing custom grant-type factory implementations at compile time and can cause AbstractMethodError at runtime for binary extensions. If this is required, the compatibility impact should be explicit; otherwise a default method should be provided.

findings.title: Public Context copy constructor removed
findings.body: The diff removes the public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context). This is a source and binary compatibility break for any extension code that copied an existing Context. If this type is considered stable enough for custom grant implementations, the removal should be avoided or clearly documented as a breaking change.

findings.title: Lightweight-token check depends on session-context client
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines whether the token is lightweight by calling AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient().getAttribute(...). Token creation already has a client available via TokenManager.initToken and the client session. If a caller creates an access token without setting the client in the session context, or if the context client differs from the token's client, this can throw NullPointerException or encode the wrong token type. The decision should use the client associated with the token being created.

findings.title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut but format requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc for OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut says it returns 'usually like 3-letters shortcut', but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes and decodes exactly two characters for the grant type field. Custom grant factories following this Javadoc could return three-character shortcuts, producing token IDs that cannot be parsed. The documentation should state that the shortcut must be exactly two characters.

findings.title: Lazily registered grant shortcuts can overwrite existing mappings
findings.body: Startup validates grant shortcut uniqueness by comparing the sizes of grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts. However, getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily insert mappings for grant factories discovered later without re-validating uniqueness or format. A newly discovered grant with a conflicting shortcut can silently overwrite the shortcut-to-grant mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type while still encoding successfully.
